Header: Alternaria porri Local Name: Pyaz k Jamni Dhabbay

Prevention: Apply manure to improve the vigour of the plants.
Follow long rotations with non-related crop, leaves a gap of at least 3 years between consecutive crops.
Provide good drainage to bring down the incidence of the disease.
Lower the density of transplanted crops to reduce the risk of infection.
Remove plant debris after harvest or incorporate it into the soil.
Harvest when plants are mature, and preferably during dry weather.
Monitoring: Check for spots which first appear as small, whitish sunken lesions.
Almost immediately, the spots turn brown, enlarge, and become zoned, somewhat sunken, and more or less purplish.
The lesions (spots) also occur on the leaves, flower stalks, and floral parts of seed onions.
Hot and humid climate with temperature ranging from 21 to 30°C and
RH (80 to 90%) favours the development of the disease.
Early symptoms can appear within 1 to 4 days after inoculation has occurred.
The conidia (fungus seed) are carried to other onion leaves by air currents, splashing rains, tools and so on.
Direct Control: Check plants in the nursery and remove any seedlings that show leaf spots before transfer to the field.
Remove plant debris after harvest or incorporate it into the soil so that it decomposes quickly.
Topsin-M @ 2.5 grams/1 kg seed) to save new crop from pathogen attack.
Fosetyl aluminium 80WP (Aliette) @ 250 gram/120L water/acre) followed by spraying.
Restrictions: Fungicides may be applied on a 7-day schedule, if necessary.
For all fungicides, thorough coverage of foliage is important to control the disease.
Always wear impermeable gloves, long pants & long-sleeve shirts during spray.
Change clothes and wash your hands immediately after applying pesticides.
Don't spray outdoors on windy or rainy days.
